title: Criminal Complaint: State of Wisconsin v. Tehrangi N. Chapman

reports.title: Second member of the Milwaukee Police Department charged with misuse of license plate reader system
Criminal Complaint: State of Wisconsin v. Tehrangi N. Chapman

summary:
Milwaukee Police Detective Tehrangi Chapman, a 22-year veteran assigned to internal affairs, was charged with felony misconduct in public office and misuse of a GPS device. A complaint says he admitted using the Flock license plate reader system 20 times to track two people. He allegedly searched one person's plate 17 times from January 10, 2024, to January 3, 2025, and installed a GPS device on that vehicle. He also searched another person's plate three times on January 7, 2025, listing training as the reason. He has been suspended since March 13 and is due in court July 17.

The charges follow former Officer Josue Ayala, who pleaded guilty to attempted misconduct in June and resigned after being accused of using the system to check vehicles tied to someone he dated and that person's ex. Chapman had investigated Ayala's misuse. Milwaukee's fire and police commissioner called the charges troubling, and the police chief said no one is above the law. The department has changed system access and audits. Several Wisconsin communities have ended or declined to renew Flock contracts.
